intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia-51 (SPG51) is caused by homozygous mutation in the AP4E1 gene (607244) on chromosome 15q21.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia-51 (SPG51) is caused by homozygous mutation in the AP4E1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: an autosomal recessive form of spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy with profound intellectual disability, microcephaly, epilepsy and white matter loss in a consanguineous family resulting from a homozygous deletion involving AP4E1
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous deletion that also includes part of SPPL2A, not a point mutation in AP4E1 alone. It calls the disorder cerebral palsy, not SPG51.

checks.claim: The AP4E1 gene is located on chromosome 15q21.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a 139 kb (minimum) to 222 kb (maximum) homozygous deletion of chromosome 15q21.2 that includes the 5′ end of two genes: AP4E1
checks.explanation: The paper places AP4E1 within the deleted region at 15q21.2.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia-51 is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder. It begins with neonatal or infantile hypotonia that later becomes spasticity of the limbs, often spastic tetraplegia. Other features include severe intellectual disability, poor or absent speech, microcephaly, seizures and mild facial dysmorphism. It belongs to the group of disorders caused by deficiency of the adaptor protein complex-4 (AP-4), sometimes called 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome.' Defects in the other AP-4 subunits, AP4B1, AP4M1 and AP4S1, cause clinically similar disorders.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia-51 is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Cerebral palsy is a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental brain disorders resulting in motor and posture impairments
checks.explanation: The paper describes a severe neurodevelopmental cerebral palsy syndrome.

checks.claim: SPG51 begins with neonatal or infantile hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: At birth she presented with microcephaly and hypotonia that progressed to spastic tetraplegia
checks.explanation: Neonatal hypotonia is reported in both patients.

checks.claim: In SPG51, early hypotonia later becomes spasticity of the limbs, often spastic tetraplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: At birth she presented with microcephaly and hypotonia that progressed to spastic tetraplegia with hyperreflexia and generalised hypertonia by the first year of life.
checks.explanation: The paper says the early hypotonia progressed to spastic tetraplegia.

checks.claim: SPG51 features include severe intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive form of spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy with profound intellectual disability
checks.explanation: Both patients had profound or severe intellectual disability.

checks.claim: SPG51 features include poor or absent speech.
checks.evidence_quote: He acquired some dysarthric words, but never normal speech
checks.explanation: One patient never developed speech and the other had only a few dysarthric words.

checks.claim: SPG51 features include microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Examination at age 23 showed microcephaly (−3 SD)
checks.explanation: Microcephaly is present in both patients.

checks.claim: SPG51 features include seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: Seizures started with staring spells and developed into generalised tonic-clonic at age 15.
checks.explanation: Both patients had epilepsy.

checks.claim: SPG51 features include mild facial dysmorphism.
checks.evidence_quote: Both patients presented discreet but remarkable facial gestalt with a prominent, bulbous nose, a wide mouth and coarse features.
checks.explanation: The paper reports mild facial dysmorphism.

checks.claim: SPG51 belongs to the group of disorders caused by deficiency of the adaptor protein complex-4 (AP-4), sometimes called 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome.'
checks.evidence_quote: disruption of any one of the four subunits of AP-4 causes dysfunction of the entire complex, leading to a distinct 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome'
checks.explanation: The paper introduces the term 'AP-4 deficiency syndrome'.

checks.claim: Defects in the other AP-4 subunits, AP4B1, AP4M1, and AP4S1, cause disorders clinically similar to SPG51.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified one mutation in each of three genes encoding adaptor protein complex 4 (AP4) subunits
checks.explanation: The paper reports mutations in AP4S1, AP4B1 and AP4E1 causing the same syndrome, and notes that AP4M1 mutations cause cerebral palsy with severe intellectual disability.

paragraphs.text: The disorder was first called spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy-4 (CPSQ4). Because it is progressive and classed with the hereditary spastic paraplegias, it was renamed SPG51.

checks.claim: SPG51 was first called spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy-4 (CPSQ4).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The paper does not mention the name CPSQ4.

checks.claim: CPSQ4 was renamed SPG51 because the disorder is progressive and is classed with the hereditary spastic paraplegias.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The paper does not discuss renaming the disorder SPG51 or classing it with the hereditary spastic paraplegias.

paragraphs.text: Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) described a consanguineous family in which several members had a cerebral palsy-like syndrome. Features included spastic quadriplegia, microcephaly and severe intellectual disability. Some patients also had seizures.

checks.claim: Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) described a consanguineous family in which several members had a cerebral palsy-like syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: We evaluated a Palestinian–Jordanian consanguineous family with two siblings affected by an idiopathic neurological condition described as cerebral palsy
checks.explanation: Only two siblings were affected, which is not 'several' members.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family described by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) had spastic quadriplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: On examination at 22 years, he had spastic tetraplegia with hypertonia and hyperreflexia
checks.explanation: Both patients had spastic tetraplegia (quadriplegia).

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family described by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) had microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: Postnatally he presented with microcephaly and hypotonia
checks.explanation: Both patients had microcephaly.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family described by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) had severe intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Severe cognitive deficits were noted, as well as adaptive impairments, with all age equivalents <1 year of age.
checks.explanation: Both patients had severe or profound intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Some affected members of the consanguineous family described by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) had seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: has been wheelchair-bound since 5 years of age, when she also started experiencing generalised tonic-clonic seizures
checks.explanation: Both affected patients had seizures (epilepsy + in both in table 1), so 'some' understates it.

paragraphs.text: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) reported consanguineous families with AP-4 deficiency, including a family with AP4E1 mutation. Affected individuals had severe intellectual disability, absent or minimal speech, early hypotonia that developed into progressive spasticity, and short stature. Some also had microcephaly and seizures.

checks.claim: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) reported consanguineous families with AP-4 deficiency, including a family with an AP4E1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: eight affected individuals who were from three consanguineous families
checks.explanation: There are three consanguineous families, one of them with an AP4E1 splice mutation.

checks.claim: Affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had severe intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with severe intellectual disability, absent speech
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: Affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had absent or minimal speech.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with severe intellectual disability, absent speech
checks.explanation: Absent speech is stated.

checks.claim: Affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had early hypotonia that developed into progressive spasticity.
checks.evidence_quote: muscular hypotonia that progressed to spastic paraplegia
checks.explanation: The title also calls the spastic paraplegia progressive.

checks.claim: Affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: severe autosomal-recessive intellectual disability, progressive spastic paraplegia, shy character, and short stature
checks.explanation: Short stature and growth retardation are stated.

checks.claim: Some affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: muscular hypotonia that progressed to spastic paraplegia, microcephaly, foot deformity
checks.explanation: Microcephaly is reported.

checks.claim: Some affected individuals with AP-4 deficiency reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) had seizures.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention seizures.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of SPG51 in the families reported by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) and Abou Jamra et al. (2011) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of SPG51 in the family reported by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: This report describes an autosomal recessive form of spastic tetraplegic cerebral palsy
checks.explanation: The paper reports autosomal recessive inheritance, with carrier parents and homozygous affected children.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of SPG51 in the family reported by Abou Jamra et al. (2011) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Adaptor protein complex 4 deficiency causes severe autosomal-recessive intellectual disability
checks.explanation: The disorder is autosomal recessive and occurs in consanguineous families.

paragraphs.text: Clinically similar autosomal recessive disorders are caused by mutation in the genes for the other subunits of the AP-4 complex: AP4B1 (SPG47), AP4M1 (SPG50) and AP4S1 (SPG52).

checks.claim: Mutation in AP4B1, which encodes a subunit of the AP-4 complex, causes a clinically similar autosomal recessive disorder, SPG47.
checks.evidence_quote: mutations of the four genes encoding the subunits of the AP-4 (adaptor protein-4) complex have recently been identified in patients with autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia [4], [5], [6], [7], [8], [9]. The four subunits of the AP-4 complex have the following OMIM (http://omim.org/) classifications: AP4B1, SPG47
checks.explanation: AP4B1 is an AP-4 subunit gene linked to SPG47, an autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia, and the discussion notes the shared phenotype.

checks.claim: Mutation in AP4M1, which encodes a subunit of the AP-4 complex, causes a clinically similar autosomal recessive disorder, SPG50.
checks.evidence_quote: The four subunits of the AP-4 complex have the following OMIM (http://omim.org/) classifications: AP4B1, SPG47 (OMIM*614066); AP4M1, SPG50 (OMIM*612936)
checks.explanation: AP4M1 is linked to SPG50, and the paper describes these as autosomal recessive spastic paraplegias with a shared phenotype.

checks.claim: Mutation in AP4S1, which encodes a subunit of the AP-4 complex, causes a clinically similar autosomal recessive disorder, SPG52.
checks.evidence_quote: AP4E1 SPG51 (OMIM*613744) and AP4S1, SPG52 (OMIM*614067)
checks.explanation: AP4S1 is linked to SPG52, and the paper describes these as autosomal recessive spastic paraplegias with a shared phenotype.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family with spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy, Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) identified a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the AP4E1 gene. The mutation segregated with the disorder in the family.

checks.claim: Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) identified a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the AP4E1 gene in affected members of a consanguineous family with spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a 139 kb (minimum) to 222 kb (maximum) homozygous deletion of chromosome 15q21.2 that includes the 5′ end of two genes: AP4E1 (adaptor related protein complex-4, epsilon-1) and SPPL2A
checks.explanation: The finding is a homozygous 192-kb deletion that also involves SPPL2A, not simply a loss-of-function mutation in AP4E1.

checks.claim: The homozygous AP4E1 loss-of-function mutation identified by Moreno-De-Luca et al. (2011) segregated with the disorder in the family.
checks.evidence_quote: FISH analysis on the mother revealed that she is a heterozygous carrier of the deletion.
checks.explanation: Both affected siblings were homozygous, the mother and unaffected sister were heterozygous, and the father was inferred to be a carrier. This is consistent with segregation.

paragraphs.text: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) studied consanguineous families with intellectual disability and spastic paraplegia. In one family they identified a homozygous truncating mutation in the AP4E1 gene. In other families of the same study they found mutations in other AP-4 subunit genes.

checks.claim: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) studied consanguineous families with intellectual disability and spastic paraplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: eight affected individuals who were from three consanguineous families and presented with severe intellectual disability
checks.explanation: The abstract describes consanguineous families with intellectual disability and spastic paraplegia.

checks.claim: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) identified a homozygous truncating mutation in the AP4E1 gene in one consanguineous family with intellectual disability and spastic paraplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: a splice mutation in AP4E1 (NM_007347.3: c.542+1_542+4delGTAA, r.421_542del, p.Glu181Glyfs(∗)20)
checks.explanation: The splice mutation causes a frameshift and truncation. Homozygosity is implied by the autozygosity mapping but is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: Abou Jamra et al. (2011) found mutations in other AP-4 subunit genes in other families in the same study.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified one mutation in each of three genes encoding adaptor protein complex 4 (AP4) subunits
checks.explanation: The other families had AP4S1 and AP4B1 mutations.
